name: Baseline
shortDescription: Call-fraud detector that fuses local Whisper transcripts, voice matching, deepfake-audio detection and LLM scam cues into a trust score.
description:
Baseline listens to both sides of a phone call and steps in when the voice or the story stops adding up, for example a cloned-voice "grandparent scam". It compares each speaker's delivery against their own earlier turns rather than a population average, and warns, alerts a trusted contact and holds transfers when signals agree.

Highlights:
- Pipeline: Silero VAD → Whisper (MLX, local) transcript, SpeechBrain ECAPA voice match, a deepfake-audio detector (WavLM + DeBERTa fine-tuned on an RTX 5090), pitch/pace/pause drift against the speaker's own baseline, and LLM + rule-based fraud patterns, fused into a trust score.
- Two-sided demo: play the client being protected, or the scammer trying to get past it. The AI caller is an LLM persona with an ElevenLabs synthetic voice.
- Every call ends with a report: transcript, per-detector signals and evidence linked to FTC scam guidance. Observations can be signed into an Ed25519 `did:key` credential that can be verified offline.
- Most of it runs on the laptop (speech-to-text, voice match, deepfake detection, caller persona via Ollama).
- Framed as hints, not verdicts: "not a lie detector", for consent-based use, with a human making the call.

Built overnight at Building from the Farm (Stanford Founders Club, SF Tech Week 2026).
